questions.stem: The right panel shows a mask and machine treating the obstruction seen on the left. By what mechanism does this therapy keep the airway open?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It sedates the patient to suppress arousals

choices.label: D
choices.text: It supplies supplemental oxygen without any pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: It electrically stimulates the diaphragm to contract

explanation.summary: CPAP maintains a positive intraluminal pressure throughout the respiratory cycle, acting as a pneumatic splint that prevents the relaxed pharyngeal soft tissues from collapsing.
explanation.whyCorrect: CPAP maintains a positive intraluminal pressure throughout the respiratory cycle, acting as a pneumatic splint that prevents the relaxed pharyngeal soft tissues from collapsing.

questions.stem: Comparing the 'during sleep' and 'obstruction' panels, what directly produces the airway blockage in obstructive sleep apnea?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collapse of relaxed pharyngeal soft tissues

choices.label: D
choices.text: A nasal polyp blocking the nasal cavity

explanation.summary: During sleep, loss of muscle tone allows the tongue base, soft palate, and uvula to fall back and occlude the pharynx, obstructing airflow despite continued respiratory effort.
explanation.whyCorrect: During sleep, loss of muscle tone allows the tongue base, soft palate, and uvula to fall back and occlude the pharynx, obstructing airflow despite continued respiratory effort.
